\chapter{Chapter02 — Correlated Gaussian Limit}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter02.NoiseStability.CorrelatedGaussianLimit
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter02.NoiseStability.CorrelatedGaussianLimit}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Correlation plane]
\lean{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003}
\label{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
\leanok
The correlation plane is $\mathbb R^2$ equipped with its usual Euclidean norm.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Correlated sign vector]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignVector}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b005
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p007-b003}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignVector}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
Given a pair of signs, form the vector in the correlation plane whose two coordinates
are the real values of those signs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Correlated sign projection]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
For $t=(t_1,t_2)\bbR^2$ and signs $,\mathbin\bbz^{\times}$, the correlated sign projection
of $t$ at $(,)$ is $t_1+t_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling the sign projection]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_smul}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedSignProjection}
\difficulty{3}
For every real scalar $a$, vector $t$ in the real two-dimensional correlation plane, and
pair of signs $(x,y)$, the projection at $a t$ is $a$ times the projection at $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign projection as an inner product]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_eq_inner}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_eq_inner}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedSignProjection, FABL.correlatedSignVector}
\difficulty{3}
For every vector $t$ in the real two-dimensional correlation plane and every pair of
signs $(x,y)$, the projection $x t_1+y t_2$ equals the inner product of $t$ with the
vector $(x,y)$, where signs are viewed as real numbers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Correlation quadratic form]
\lean{FABL.correlationQuadraticForm}
\label{FABL.correlationQuadraticForm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
For a real number $\rho$ and a point $t=(t_1,t_2)$ in the real correlation plane, the
correlation quadratic form is $t_1^2+2\rho t_1t_2+t_2^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of the correlated sign projection]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_expectation}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_expectation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF_expect_signValue_fst, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF_expect_signValue_snd, FABL.correlatedSignProjection, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_mul_const}
\difficulty{3}
For every $\rho\in[-1,1]$ and every vector $t=(t_1,t_2)$ in the real two-dimensional
correlation plane, the expected value of $X t_1+Y t_2$ under the correlated sign-pair
law with parameter $\rho$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment of the correlated sign projection]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_secondMoment}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_secondMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF_expect_signValue_mul, FABL.correlatedSignProjection, FABL.correlationQuadraticForm, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one}
\difficulty{5}
For every $\rho\in[-1,1]$ and every vector $t=(t_1,t_2)$ in the real two-dimensional
correlation plane, the expected square of $X t_1+Y t_2$ under the correlated sign-pair
law with parameter $\rho$ is $t_1^2+2\rho t_1t_2+t_2^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Correlated sign vector measure]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b005
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p007-b003}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignVector}
For a real parameter $\rho\in[-1,1]$, the correlated sign vector measure is the
probability distribution on the correlation plane obtained by mapping a sign pair drawn
according to the correlated sign-pair law with parameter $\rho$ to the vector of its two
real sign values.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling a correlated sign-vector characteristic function]
\lean{FABL.charFun_correlatedSignVectorMeasure_smul}
\label{FABL.charFun_correlatedSignVectorMeasure_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignProjection, FABL.correlatedSignProjection_eq_inner, FABL.correlatedSignProjection_smul, FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $a\in\mathbb R$, and let $t=(t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb R^2$. The
characteristic function of the correlated sign-vector measure at $at$ equals the
characteristic function at $a$ of the real projection $s_1t_1+s_2t_2$ under the
correlated sign-pair distribution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characteristic Function Expansion at Zero]
\lean{FABL.taylor_charFun_two_of_secondMoment}
\label{FABL.taylor_charFun_two_of_secondMoment}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space, measurable up to a null set,
with finite second moment, mean zero, and second moment $q$. Then, as $t\to0$, its
characteristic function satisfies $\mathbb{E}[e^{itX}]=1-qt^2/2+o(t^2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characteristic Function Limit from the Second Moment]
\lean{FABL.tendsto_charFun_inv_sqrt_mul_pow_of_secondMoment}
\label{FABL.tendsto_charFun_inv_sqrt_mul_pow_of_secondMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.taylor_charFun_two_of_secondMoment}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space, measurable up to a null set,
with finite second moment, mean zero, and second moment $q$. If $\varphi$ is its
characteristic function, then $\varphi(1/\sqrt{n})^n\to\exp(-q/2)$ as the positive
integer $n$ tends to infinity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Normalized correlated sign sum]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003
}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure}
For $\rho\in[-1,1]$ and a natural number $n$, take $n$ independent vectors, each with
the correlated sign vector distribution at parameter $\rho$, sum them, and scale the
result by $1/\sqrt n$. The resulting probability distribution on the correlation plane
is the normalized correlated sign sum measure.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characteristic function of a normalized correlated sum]
\lean{FABL.charFun_normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\label{FABL.charFun_normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $t\in\mathbb R^2$. The
characteristic function of the measure of the normalized sum of $n$ independent
correlated sign vectors, with normalization $1/\sqrt n$, at $t$ equals $\displaystyle
\left(\varphi\left(t/\sqrt n\right)\right)^n$, where $\varphi$ is the characteristic
function of one correlated sign-vector measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian correlation map]
\lean{FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b004
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002}
\label{FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
For each real number $\rho$, define a map from $\mathbb R^2$ to the correlation plane by
sending $(u,v)$ to $(u,\rho u+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,v)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Continuity of the Gaussian correlation map]
\lean{FABL.continuous_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\label{FABL.continuous_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
\difficulty{1}
For each real number $\\rho$, define a map on the real plane equipped with the $2$-norm
by $(u,v)\\mapsto (u,\\rho u+\\sqrt{1-\\rho^2}\\,v)$. This map is continuous.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Correlated Gaussian measure]
\lean{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b004
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002}
\label{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.continuous_gaussianCorrelationMap, FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
For a real parameter $\rho$, let $\gamma$ be the probability measure on $\mathbb R^2$
obtained as the pushforward of the product of two independent standard Gaussian measures
under the Gaussian correlation map with parameter $\rho$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Inner product of Gaussian correlation images]
\lean{FABL.inner_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\label{FABL.inner_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $\rho$, every pair $(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, and every vector $t$ in
the real correlation plane, the inner product of the Gaussian correlation image of
$(u,v)$ with $t$ is $u$ times the sum of the first coordinate of $t$ and $\rho$ times
its second coordinate, plus $v$ times $\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$ times the second coordinate of
$t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characteristic function of a correlated Gaussian]
\lean{FABL.charFun_correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\label{FABL.charFun_correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.continuous_gaussianCorrelationMap, FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure, FABL.correlationQuadraticForm, FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap, FABL.inner_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $t=(t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb R^2$. The characteristic function of
the correlated Gaussian probability measure with correlation parameter $\rho$, evaluated
at $t$, is $\displaystyle \exp\!\left(-\frac{t_1^2+2\rho t_1t_2+t_2^2}{2}\right)$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
For a real correlation parameter $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $\mu_n$ be the law on $\mathbb
R^2$ of $n^{-1/2}$ times the sum of $n$ independent, identically distributed pairs of
signs, where each pair has uniform first coordinate and its second coordinate is
obtained by keeping the first with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and otherwise reversing it.
As $n\to\infty$, the probability measures $\mu_n$ converge weakly to the centered
bivariate Gaussian law with unit marginal variances and correlation $\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Pairwise coordinate correspondence]
\lean{FABL.pairCoordinatesEquiv}
\label{FABL.pairCoordinatesEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For each nonnegative integer $n$, pairs of sign vectors of length $n$ are in bijection
with functions assigning a pair of signs to each of the $n$ coordinates. The
correspondence pairs the two signs at each coordinate, and its inverse recovers the two
sign vectors from those coordinatewise pairs.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Independent coordinate decomposition]
\lean{FABL.correlatedPairPMF_map_pairCoordinatesEquiv}
\label{FABL.correlatedPairPMF_map_pairCoordinatesEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlatedPairPMF_apply, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF_apply, FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.independentProductPMF_apply, FABL.noiseKernel, FABL.pairCoordinatesEquiv, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $\rho\in[-1,1]$. For a correlated pair $(X,Y)$ of sign vectors
in $\{\pm1\}^n$, formed by choosing $X$ uniformly and applying independent coordinate
noise with retention probability $(1+\rho)/2$, rearrange the pair as
$((X_i,Y_i))_{i=1}^n$. Its law is the product of $n$ copies of the law of a single sign
pair formed by choosing the first sign uniformly from $\{\pm1\}$ and applying the same
noise rule to obtain the second.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Measure of an independent product distribution]
\lean{FABL.independentProductPMF_toMeasure}
\label{FABL.independentProductPMF_toMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.independentProductPMF_apply}
\difficulty{3}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, and let $A_i$ be a finite measurable space for each $i\in
I$, with every singleton measurable. For a probability mass function $p_i$ on each
$A_i$, the measure associated with their independent product distribution equals the
product measure of the associated coordinate measures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Normalized correlated sign-vector sum]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignVectorSum}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003
}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignVectorSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedSignVector}
For $n\in\mathbb N$ and a sequence $z$ of length $n$ whose entries are pairs of signs,
take the sum of the correlated sign vectors associated with its entries and multiply by
$1/\sqrt n$. The result lies in the two-dimensional Euclidean plane.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Normalized sum of correlated sign vectors]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003
}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignVectorSum, FABL.pairCoordinatesEquiv}
For $n\in\mathbb N$ and a pair $(x,y)$ of sign vectors in $\{-1,1\}^n$, define their
normalized correlated pair sum to be the normalized sum of correlated sign vectors
obtained by reindexing the coordinates of $(x,y)$ into paired coordinates. The result
lies in the two-dimensional Euclidean plane.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of normalized sum distributions]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure_eq_map_correlatedPairPMF}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure_eq_map_correlatedPairPMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlatedPairPMF_map_pairCoordinatesEquiv, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignVector, FABL.independentProductPMF_toMeasure, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure, FABL.pairCoordinatesEquiv}
\difficulty{3}
Let $-1\leq \rho\leq 1$ and let $n$ be a natural number. The probability measure
obtained by taking $n$ independent correlated pairs of signs, mapping each pair to its
point in the plane, summing those points, and dividing by $\sqrt n$ equals the
distribution of the normalized pair sum when the first sign vector is uniform and each
coordinate of the second is kept with probability $(1+\rho)/2$.
\end{theorem}
